title: Accuracy of measurements

match.reason: No point in the bank covers measurement error or limits of accuracy, so this needs a new point.

draft.title: Accuracy of measurements
card: No measurement is exact. An instrument can only show readings to its smallest unit, such as 1 mm on a ruler.
half the smallest unit on the instrument. A ruler marked in 1 mm steps has an absolute error of 0.5 mm.
the measurement minus the absolute error, up to the measurement plus the absolute error. The true value lies between these limits.
Example: a length is 24 cm, read from a ruler marked in whole centimetres. Absolute error = 1 ÷ 2 = 0.5 cm. Limits: 24 − 0.5 = 23.5 cm to 24 + 0.5 = 24.5 cm.
draft.remember: Absolute error is half the smallest unit. Limits are the reading plus and minus it.

a.q: A kitchen scale shows masses in steps of 2 g. What is its absolute error?
a.why: The absolute error is half the smallest unit, and 2 ÷ 2 = 1 g. Choosing 2 g is tempting, but that is the whole smallest unit, not half of it.
a.clue: Halve the size of the smallest step.

b.q: Priya measures a plank as 3.4 m, using a tape marked in steps of 0.1 m. What are the limits of accuracy?
b.why: The absolute error is 0.1 ÷ 2 = 0.05 m. So the limits are 3.4 − 0.05 = 3.35 m and 3.4 + 0.05 = 3.45 m. The range 3.3 m to 3.5 m uses the whole smallest unit instead of half.
b.clue: Halve 0.1 first, then subtract and add it.
